title: 3D Surface Imaging in Orthognathic Surgery: Retrospective Anthropometric Analysis and FRS Evaluation
summary:
Surgical correction of jaw deformities (“orthognathic surgery”) affects not only the skeletal structures but also the appearance of the face, particularly in the regions of the nose, lips, and mouth. In this retrospective study, image data from 59 patients treated at the University Hospital Regensburg are analyzed. The dataset consists of existing three-dimensional facial images (3D stereophotogrammetry, Vectra M5) as well as radiographs.

Using predefined anatomical landmarks, parameters such as nasal width, mouth width, lip projection, and the nasolabial angle are measured and compared before and after surgery. The aim of the study is to systematically document typical soft tissue changes following orthognathic surgery.

interventions.name: Patients who underwent surgical correction of dentofacial deformities (orthognathic surgery) at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, University Hospital Regensburg, between January 22, 2016, and February 26, 2020.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients from the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, University Hospital Regensburg, who underwent orthognathic surgery between 2016 and 2020 are included.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients will be excluded if complete pre- and postoperative 3D surface images are not available or if image quality is insufficient (e.g., artifacts, non-neutral head position, missing landmarks). Further exclusion criteria include incomplete surgical documentation, or missing demographic data.
